description:
ABOUT BRACKET BOT

Robots today are where computers were when they filled a room: expensive, hard to use, and run by specialists.

 

We’re making the one anyone can afford. That means designing all of it ourselves: the parts, the boards, the connectors, the software and the ML.

 

Then we put our robots to work in the real world to learn what they need next.

 

We’re backed by Fifty Years (Scott Phoenix), BoxGroup, SV Angel, Betaworks, Pace Capital, and angels including Nat Friedman, Logan Kilpatrick (Google AI), Guillermo Rauch (Vercel) and others from Tesla AI, Physical Intelligence, and Markforged.

 
 


ABOUT THE ROLE

People keep asking us for a robot at their place. Until now, the honest answer to “what’s stopping you?” was: one of us has to go there and make it work.

 

That can’t scale. It’s as if every Waymo needed an engineer in the driver’s seat to learn each new road. A robot that needs an engineer to learn a new job will never be in a million places, and that’s where we’re going.

 

This role is the bridge. A robot comes off our line, goes somewhere it has never been, and does a job nobody has taught it yet. You make that happen, and then you make it happen without you. Everything that made it hard goes back into the robot, the software and how we set up, until a new place takes an afternoon, and then no one.

 
 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Take a new job from “could a robot do this?” to a robot doing it every day.

 - Get robots working in homes, offices, shops and factories, and run the first shifts yourself, by teleoperation if that’s what it takes.

 - Turn those first shifts into the data and tools that let the robot do the job alone.

 - Fix whatever breaks: software, a camera, a gripper, the Wi-Fi.

 - Decide with us which jobs come next.

 


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - You’ve made a robot do something useful outside a lab, and kept it working.

 - You can go from a Python script to a crimped cable to a reprinted part in one afternoon.

 - You’d rather fix the cause than go back twice.

 - You like being where the robot is, with the people who need it.

 - Years of experience matter less than what you’ve made.

 


NICE TO HAVE

 - Teleoperation, imitation learning, navigation or robot arms.

 - Robotics competitions or design teams.

 


HOW TO APPLY

Apply at bracketbot.com/apply https://bracketbot.com/apply. It takes a name or a link and about ten seconds: no resume, no form. One application covers every role, and we match you to one during interviews. The Apply button on this page works too.

 

The process is a 15-minute call, a review of your past work, then a work trial of two to five days with us in San Francisco. The job is onsite in San Francisco, with travel to where the robots work. You don’t need to live here yet.

 

Bracket Bot is an equal opportunity employer. We’re building a diverse team and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.
